source_notes.label: Distinct structural dimensions
source_notes.summary: The authors report approximately 7 ± 1 nm CdS particles, approximately 20 nm sharp-edged aggregates, approximately 8.2 nm Scherrer grains and approximately 150 nm film thickness. These describe different objects and are not interchangeable. The statistic represented by ±1 nm is not identified.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Film preparation, Figure 1 and structural discussion

source_notes.label: Crystallinity is qualified
source_notes.summary: SAED has diffuse rings, which the authors associate with significant amorphous and/or less nanocrystalline structure. Indexed (100)/(002) planes and preferential [100]/[002] growth are reported; no explicit polymorph name, unit-cell constants or coordinates are provided here.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 1 and structural discussion

source_notes.label: Hydrophilic interface is the proposed advantage
source_notes.summary: Quaternary pyridinium salts render the otherwise hydrophobic conjugated polymers water-soluble. The authors argue that compatible hydrophilic surfaces improve sensitizer contact with CdS. The measured bare-film water contact angle is about 15 degrees; the introduction’s less-than-10-degree statement is a general background description, not this measured value.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Introduction, Figure 1d and polymer discussion

source_notes.label: Carboxyl functionality and cell response
source_notes.summary: LM 3 has greater measured adsorption than LM 2 and higher reported cell efficiency. The authors attribute this to carboxyl-mediated electronic coupling and improved electron transfer. This is their interpretation; adsorption density, optical tail and cell performance are retained as distinct evidence, not direct structural proof of a particular surface bond.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 3, Figure 4 and Table I

source_notes.label: Energy conventions remain as printed
source_notes.summary: The source gives positive LUMO values of 3.23 and 3.42 eV with normal hydrogen electrode for LM 2/LM 3, and a CdS conduction-band value of 4.2 eV in its interpretation. The underlying CV curves are not shown. The values are not converted to vacuum energies, sign-corrected or treated as new measured CdS band levels.
